name: HACHI-HACHI (八八)
description: Hachi-Hachi (八八, '88') is the most representative Japanese Hanafuda fishing game. The name refers to the par score of 88 points (one-third of the 264 total points in the deck). Played by 3-6 players with a bidding phase to determine the three active players each round. Features complex scoring with teyaku (initial hand combinations) and deki-yaku (combinations formed during play). Players can stop early if they form valuable combinations.

content.text: Hachi-Hachi (八八, '88') is the most representative Japanese Hanafuda fishing game. The name refers to the par score of 88 points (one-third of the 264 total points in the deck). Played by 3-6 players with a bidding phase to determine the three active players each round. Features complex scoring with teyaku (initial hand combinations) and deki-yaku (combinations formed during play). Players can stop early if they form valuable combinations.
Traditional Japanese game using Hanafuda (flower cards), which originated in the 18th century. Hachi-Hachi is considered the most representative Hanafuda fishing game.
3-6 players. Only 3 play actively each round; others sit out after bidding.
Two denominations of chips: 'Kan' and 'Mon' (1 Kan = 12 Mon typically).
Deal cards to the 3 active players. Place cards face-up in the center (the 'field').
